speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; to begin my evaluation, have you noticed any recent injury, insect bites, or changes in color or temperature in that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of your finger getting caught in a jersey and pulled forcefully suggests a possible tendon injury. Can you tell me if you were able to straighten your finger after the injury, or if it feels like the tendon has snapped?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (Extensor Tendon Ruptation).

The inability to actively flex the distal interphalangeal joint combined with pain, swelling, and the finger resting in extension after a forced hyperextension injury is classic for this diagnosis.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
